Subject: Redwood integration — retention details and evidence request

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick demo today — we got the integration running in our staging tenant. Our audit team has two outstanding asks before we move to a production permit:

1) A concise table showing which telemetry and debug traces Redwood persists for tenant-scoped sessions (session start/end, prompt/response KV indexes, model selection metadata) and the retention TTLs for each (default and configurable values).
2) For ephemeral session traces used for debugging (debug snapshots / trace fragments), we need a customer-specific exception path: can you describe how a Proofpoint workspace could request a temporary extension (30/90 days) and what compensating controls (sealed export, encrypted snapshot, access logging) Redwood would apply?

Can you provide the retention matrix and any signed evidence artifacts (hashed manifests or Exhibit A) we can attach to our SIG submission? Ideally we need something we can upload to our risk portal by EOD Thu (two business days).

Best,
Maria Lopez
Security Engineer — Integrations
Proofpoint

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (security evidence) and Priyom (customer retention flows) to pull the artifacts.

Short answers up front:
- We keep tenant-scoped session metadata (session_id, model, routing variant, timestamps) for 30 days by default; debug snapshots (full ephemeral traces) are 7 days by default. Both are configurable per-customer for Dedicated/Private customers via a support request and policy handoff.
- Temporary extensions are supported: customers file a retention-extension request (work order) and we create a sealed export stored in our evidence bucket with HSM-wrapped keys, strict ACLs, and an audit entry. We can support 30/90-day extensions; anything longer requires legal review.

We will produce: retention matrix (spreadsheet), an evidence manifest with SHA256 checksums, and a short playbook describing the extension request workflow and compensating controls. Expect a package by EOD Wed.

-JW
Jonas Weber
Head of Platform Security (on-call)
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Retention matrix and evidence manifest (draft)

Jonas / Priyom — attaching the working spreadsheet and the manifest. Key notes included inline in the sheet:

- Columns: artifact_type, default_ttl_days, max_ttl_with_extension_days, access_controls, storage_class, evidence_hash
- Ephemeral debug snapshots: default 7d, extension up to 90d via support ticket; extension flow: ticket -> legal & security approval -> sealed export -> access tokens scoped to Proofpoint SSO group for duration -> automated deletion at expiry.
- Tenant session metadata (non-PHI): default 30d, configurable to 365d for Dedicated/Private with contractual SLA.
- Keystore rotation logs: retained 90 days for audit; immutable snapshots are placed under key-escrow for 7 years when customer requests legal hold.

I included an example sealed export manifest entry and a sample HSM-wrapped key fingerprint (SHA256: 3f7e...b9c2).

Attaching: redwood_retention_matrix_2026-08.xlsx; draft_manifest_v1.txt (hashes).

- Ben
